name: Salzburg
tagline: Baroque city of Mozart between fortress and alpine foothills
bestMonths: Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep
whenBlurb: Summer belongs to the Salzburg Festival in July and August; December's Advent markets are pure enchantment and January brings Mozart Week, avoid only the grey, quiet late winter.

ourTake.lede: Salzburg is small and easily walked, so give it a couple of unhurried days rather than a rushed one, the Altstadt is the attraction, best seen early or late when the tour groups thin. It lives and breathes music; if you can align with the summer Festival or Mozart Week in January, do, because that's when the city is fully itself. Skip the Sound of Music bus tours unless that's genuinely your thing, and instead take the funicular up to the fortress for the view and a slow lunch.
ourTake.comeIf: You want Mozart, baroque streets and the Alps rising at the edge of a small city.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a big-city buzz; Salzburg is compact and best taken slowly.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Rosewood Schloss Fuschl
items.area: Hof bei Salzburg / Lake Fuschl (≈25 min east of the Old Town)
items.description: A 15th-century lakeside castle reborn by Rosewood in 2024, the region's most complete luxury retreat, set in its own estate on Lake Fuschl.

items.name: Hotel Sacher Salzburg
items.area: Neustadt / right bank, on the Salzach facing the Old Town
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Salzburg's grande dame, a riverside palace of the famed Sacher family, with the finest Old Town views in the city.

items.name: Hotel Schloss Mönchstein
items.area: Mönchsberg / the city mountain, above the Old Town
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A small castle-hotel in a private park atop the Mönchsberg, seclusion and forest quiet, minutes above the city by the mountain lift.

items.name: Hotel Goldener Hirsch, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.area: Altstadt / Getreidegasse, the heart of the Old Town
items.description: An inn since 1564 on Salzburg's grandest shopping street, beamed, antique-filled rooms with centuries of pedigree, now under Marriott's Luxury Collection.

items.name: Hotel Bristol Salzburg
items.description: A grand 1892 house of imperial guests and a private art collection, old-world Salzburg beside the Mirabell Gardens.

items.name: Sheraton Grand Salzburg
items.description: A capable, spacious modern grand hotel right on the Mirabell Gardens, reliable comfort and easy access to both riverbanks.

items.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: One of the largest and best-preserved medieval fortresses in Europe, begun in 1077 and never once taken by siege, crowning the city on its rock. A private guide can time the reserved funicular ride so grandparents skip the climb, and the ramparts give the family the definitive photograph of Salzburg spread below.

items.name: FestungsBahn Funicular
items.description: One of the world's oldest operating funiculars, running up to the fortress since 1892 on the line of an even older 16th-century hoist. The 54-second ride spares elders and small children the steep cobbled walk and is a small delight in itself.

items.name: The Old Town (Altstadt)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg
items.description: A tight weave of Baroque squares, archways and merchant courtyards between the fortress and the river, walkable end to end and closed to most traffic. A private walking guide turns it from a pretty maze into a legible story of prince-archbishops, Mozart and money.

items.name: Getreidegasse
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Salzburg's famous shopping lane, narrow and canyon-like, hung with wrought-iron guild signs that even global luxury houses must obey. The address of Mozart's birthplace at number 9 and a good spot to combine boutiques with a discreet, unhurried browse.

items.name: Mozart's Birthplace (Mozarts Geburtshaus)
items.description: The yellow house where Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in 1756 and lived his first seventeen years, now a museum of his violins, letters and portraits. The essential Mozart pilgrimage, best taken with a private guide who can bring the child prodigy vividly to life for a multi-generational group.

items.name: Mozart Residence (Mozart-Wohnhaus)
items.description: The larger apartment across the river where the Mozart family moved in 1773, with the composer's own fortepiano and a quieter, more reflective feel than the crowded birthplace. The two houses together give the fuller portrait of the man behind the myth.

items.name: Salzburg Cathedral (Dom)
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The vast early-Baroque cathedral where Mozart was baptised and later served as organist, its bronze doors, marble facade and 4,000-pipe organs setting the scale of the prince-archbishops' ambition. Cool, grand and free to enter for a moment of calm between sights.

items.name: DomQuartier Salzburg
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: A single connected circuit through the Residenz state rooms, the cathedral terrace and galleries, and St Peter's museum, the seat of church-and-state power reopened after two centuries closed. A rewarding, weather-proof morning with a private guide for a family that wants depth over crowds.

items.name: Residenz State Rooms
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The prince-archbishops' city palace, a suite of gilded staterooms where the young Mozart performed for the court, hung with Rembrandt, Rubens and Titian in the adjoining gallery. Opulent and intimate, the private face of Salzburg's rulers.

items.name: St Peter's Abbey (Stift St. Peter)
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: Founded in 696, the oldest monastery in the German-speaking world, its abbey church a layered jewel of Romanesque bones dressed in Rococo. Still a working Benedictine community, quiet and deeply atmospheric.

items.name: St Peter's Cemetery (Petersfriedhof)
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: One of Salzburg's oldest burial grounds, a wrought-iron garden of arcaded family vaults set against the sheer Mönchsberg cliff, where Mozart's sister Nannerl rests, and the visual model for The Sound of Music's escape scene. Serene, exquisite and endlessly photogenic.

items.name: Catacombs of St Peter
items.description: Early Christian chapels and hermit cells hewn straight into the rock face above the cemetery, reached by a steep stair to little rooms with a startling view down over the graves. A short, memorable climb for those steady on their feet.

items.name: Nonnberg Abbey (Stift Nonnberg)
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The oldest continuously operating convent in the German-speaking world, founded around 714, where the real Maria von Trapp was a novice before her marriage. A hushed, working nunnery just above the Old Town, and the true starting point of the Sound of Music story.

items.name: Franciscan Church (Franziskanerkirche)
items.description: A quietly extraordinary church where a dark Romanesque nave opens into a soaring Gothic choir crowned by a golden Baroque high altar, three eras stacked in one space. Often overlooked between the bigger sights, and all the better for it.

items.name: Mirabell Palace and Gardens
credentials: Part of the Historic Centre of the City of Salzburg UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: A palace built by a prince-archbishop for his mistress, its geometric Baroque gardens framing the Pegasus fountain and the fortress beyond, the Do-Re-Mi steps of The Sound of Music. Free, beautifully kept and effortless for elders and children, best at golden hour when the crowds thin.

items.name: Marble Hall (Marmorsaal), Mirabell
items.description: The former archbishop's banqueting hall, a jewel-box of marble, stucco and fresco where Mozart played as a boy and where intimate chamber concerts are still given by candlelight. One of the loveliest small concert rooms in Europe and a romantic private-evening option.

items.name: Mozart Dinner Concert at St Peter Stiftskulinarium
credentials: St Peter Stiftskulinarium, one of the oldest restaurants in Europe (records from 803 AD)
items.description: A candlelit evening of Mozart arias and a period three-course dinner in the Baroque hall of Europe's oldest restaurant, in business since 803 and once graced by Mozart himself. A romantic, only-in-Salzburg night; the kitchen will handle vegetarian and Indian dietary needs with advance notice.

items.name: Salzburg Festival (Salzburger Festspiele)
items.area: Festival District, Altstadt (seasonal, late July to end August)
items.description: Founded in 1920, the world's foremost festival of opera and drama, filling the Grosses Festspielhaus, the Felsenreitschule carved into the cliff, and the squares with the finest voices alive. The reason to plan a summer trip well in advance; the hardest ticket in classical music, and worth every effort to secure.

items.name: Felsenreitschule
items.description: A theatre carved into the living rock of the Mönchsberg, its stone arcades once a riding school and now a spectacular festival stage, and the concert-hall backdrop of the final Sound of Music scene. Extraordinary even empty; unforgettable during a performance.

items.name: Mozarteum Foundation (Stiftung Mozarteum)
items.description: The world's centre of Mozart scholarship, with two elegant concert halls, the family's letters and instruments, and the small garden pavilion where he is said to have composed The Magic Flute. The serious counterpoint to the tourist Mozart, for those who want the real music.

items.name: Museum der Moderne Mönchsberg
items.description: A crisp modernist gallery of 20th- and 21st-century art set 60 metres above the Old Town, reached by a dedicated lift that rises in half a minute. The art is strong, but the terrace and its restaurant hold the finest full panorama of the city and Alps, a serene lunch with a view.

items.name: Mönchsberg Walk and Viewpoints
items.description: A green cliff-top promenade running the length of the Old Town, dotted with lookouts, the Richterhöhe bastion and quiet benches, easily reached by lift and level once you are up. The locals' escape from the crowds below, with the fortress on one side and the mountains on the other.

items.name: Kapuzinerberg
items.description: The wooded hill facing the fortress, climbed by a Stations-of-the-Cross path to a Capuchin monastery, deer, and some of the best views back at the Old Town skyline. Stefan Zweig once lived here; a peaceful, uncrowded hour for those who like to walk.

items.name: Salzach Riverbanks
items.description: Wide, flat promenades along the fast green river linking the two halves of the city, lined with pastel facades and lace-locked footbridges, the fortress always in view. The easiest, loveliest stroll in Salzburg, perfect for a multi-generational group at any pace.

items.name: Salzburg Museum (Neue Residenz)
credentials: European Museum of the Year Award winner (2009)
items.description: The city's flagship history museum in the New Residence palace, elegantly telling Salzburg's story from Roman roots through the prince-archbishops to the Festival. An award-winning, unhurried indoor option when the weather turns.

items.name: Hellbrunn Palace and Trick Fountains
items.description: A prince-archbishop's 1615 pleasure villa surrounded by Mannerist water gardens engineered to soak unsuspecting guests, grottoes, a hydraulic mechanical theatre and hidden jets that delight children and grandparents alike. A joyous, easy half-day just outside town; take a private guide who knows which seats stay dry.

items.name: The Sound of Music Gazebo (Hellbrunn)
items.description: The glass garden pavilion of "Sixteen Going on Seventeen," moved to the Hellbrunn grounds and freely visitable in the park. A quick, sentimental stop that pairs naturally with the trick fountains for fans of the film.

items.name: Steintheater (Stone Theatre), Hellbrunn
credentials: Oldest open-air opera stage north of the Alps (first performance 1617)
items.description: A former quarry turned open-air stage, where in 1617 the first opera performed outside Italy was staged, arguably the oldest such theatre north of the Alps. A hidden, moss-softened amphitheatre a short walk from the palace, magical and almost always empty.

items.name: Sound of Music Locations Tour
items.description: The half-day circuit of film settings, Leopoldskron's lake terrace, Frohnburg's gates, the Mirabell gardens, the Nonnberg convent and the Mondsee wedding church. Best done privately by car so the family sets its own pace and skips the sing-along coach.

items.name: Schloss Leopoldskron
items.description: A Rococo lakeside palace, once Max Reinhardt's and the lake-terrace "von Trapp villa" of The Sound of Music, now an exclusive private hotel and seminar house. Its mirrored Venetian Room and gardens can be experienced over afternoon tea or a stay, the film's most beautiful real address.

items.name: Stiegl-Brauwelt
items.description: The visitor world of Austria's largest private brewery, brewing since 1492, with a museum, a garden and generous tastings of unfiltered beer. A relaxed, hands-on afternoon for the beer-curious and an easy change of register from all the Baroque.

items.name: Untersberg Cable Car
items.area: St. Leonhard, south of the city
items.description: An eight-minute glass gondola from the city's doorstep to the top of the Untersberg at 1,776 metres, where a short walk delivers a sweeping Alpine panorama across Salzburg and Bavaria. The quickest way to put the family on a real mountain summit before lunch, take warm layers even in summer.

items.name: Gaisberg
items.description: The rounded local mountain reached by a scenic road to a summit of paragliders, walking trails and a 360-degree view over the lakes and Alps. A favourite short drive for locals at sunset, and gentle enough for a stroll rather than a hike.

items.name: Hallstatt
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Hallstatt-Dachstein / Salzkammergut Cultural Landscape
items.description: The impossibly pretty lake-and-mountain village whose reflected houses have made it one of Europe's most photographed places, with a 7,000-year salt-mining history above it. Go early or late to have it calm; a private driver makes the scenic Wolfgangsee route part of the pleasure.

items.name: St Wolfgang and the Wolfgangsee
items.description: A storybook lakeside village around the White Horse Inn of operetta fame, with a rack railway up the Schafberg for a panorama over the whole lake district. A relaxed, elegant stop on the way to or from Hallstatt, with lake terraces made for a long lunch.

items.name: Fuschlsee and Fuschl am See
items.description: A small, dazzlingly clear drinking-water lake ringed by forest, closest of the lakes to the city and home to the Schloss Fuschl estate. An easy first taste of the Salzkammergut, a swim, a lakeside walk, and back for dinner.

items.name: Königssee and St Bartholomä
items.description: A fjord-like emerald lake beneath the sheer Watzmann massif, crossed by silent electric boats to the onion-domed pilgrimage chapel of St Bartholomä. Among the most beautiful lakes in the Alps and a serene, easy outing, passports for the border, though it is a formality within Europe.

items.name: Eagle's Nest (Kehlsteinhaus)
items.description: A stone lodge on a 1,834-metre ridge above Berchtesgaden, built in 1938 and reached by a dramatic mountain road and a brass-lined lift through the rock, now a viewpoint restaurant over the Alps. A sobering piece of history with an extraordinary panorama; open roughly mid-May to October.

items.name: Salzwelten Salt Mine, Hallein
credentials: Oldest salt mine in the world still shown to visitors
items.description: The salt that made Salzburg rich, explored underground on miners' wooden slides, a boat across a mirror-still brine lake and a train through the mountain, theatrical fun that lands equally with children and grandparents. Cool year-round; they provide the overalls.

items.name: Eisriesenwelt Ice Cave, Werfen
credentials: Largest ice cave in the world open to visitors
items.description: The largest ice cave in the world open to visitors, over 40 kilometres of passages with about a kilometre of glittering frozen cathedrals and waterfalls lit by carbide lamp. A genuine adventure, cold, with steps and a cable car, best for the fitter and more curious of the group.

items.name: Hohenwerfen Fortress, Werfen
items.description: A 900-year-old cliff-top castle above the Salzach valley, famous for its dramatic falconry demonstrations with eagles and vultures wheeling over the ramparts. It stars in the aerial shots of The Sound of Music, and pairs naturally with the nearby ice cave for a full mountain day.

items.name: Grossglockner High Alpine Road
items.area: Hohe Tauern (day trip, ~1.5–2 hr; seasonal, May–Oct)
items.description: One of Europe's great scenic drives, a ribbon of hairpins climbing past 2,500 metres to face Austria's highest peak and the Pasterze glacier, with marmots and ibex on the high meadows. A full day best done with a private driver so the family simply watches the Alps unfold.

items.name: Krimml Waterfalls
items.area: Hohe Tauern (day trip, ~2 hr; seasonal, May–Oct)
items.description: The highest waterfalls in Austria, a 380-metre triple cascade thundering through pine forest, climbed by a well-graded switchback path with viewing platforms at each tier. A refreshing Alpine outing; the lower falls reward even a gentle half-hour stroll.

items.name: Berchtesgaden Salt Mine
items.description: A working German salt mine turned experience, entered by mine train and slides with a light show across an underground salt lake, a polished alternative to Hallein just over the border. Reliably delightful for children, and cool on a hot summer afternoon.

items.name: Restaurant Ikarus
items.area: Hangar-7, by the airport (≈10 min from the Old Town)
items.description: The world's only rotating-guest-chef fine-dining room, a different acclaimed chef every month, under culinary director Martin Klein, inside Red Bull's glass Hangar-7.

items.name: SENNS.Restaurant
items.area: Söllheim / a converted metal factory on the city's edge
items.description: Andreas Senn's precise, contemporary cooking in a raw industrial hall, Salzburg's other two-star, and one of Austria's most exciting tables.

items.name: Restaurant Obauer
items.description: The Obauer brothers' legendary two-star, a lifetime of refined alpine-Austrian cooking, worth the drive out toward the Werfen ice caves.

items.name: Carpe Diem
items.description: Fine dining reimagined as elegant, cone-served small plates, a singular concept on the Old Town's grandest street, from the Red Bull stable.

items.name: Esszimmer
items.area: Neustadt / at the foot of the Mönchsberg
items.description: Andreas Kaiblinger's flavour-forward, contemporary Austrian cooking, with his wife Andrea's warm front-of-house and a considered wine list.

items.name: The Glass Garden
items.description: Simon Wagner's delicate, produce-led cooking in a glass pavilion high above the city, food and fortress views in one sitting.

items.name: Pfefferschiff
items.area: Hallwang / Söllheim (≈15 min north-east of the Old Town)
items.description: Jürgen Vigne's bold, ingredient-driven cooking in a 17th-century parish house, one of the region's longest-running serious kitchens.

items.name: Restaurant Brandstätter
items.area: Salzburg / Liefering, west of the centre
items.description: A family-run country house of hearty, honest Austrian cooking, a beautiful garden, a serious cellar and terrific value.

items.name: Augustiner Bräustübl Mülln
items.description: A monastery beer hall pouring from wooden barrels since 1621, Austria's largest of its kind, all stone jugs, chestnut garden and unforced local life.

items.name: The Sketch Bar & Lounge, Hotel Bristol
items.description: The grand old Bristol's fireside bar, creative cocktails and long drinks in a calm, old-world room facing the Mirabell Gardens.

items.name: Schloss Bar, Rosewood Schloss Fuschl
items.description: The lakeside castle's handsome main bar, hand-painted alpine murals, classic and inventive cocktails, and an intimate Whisky Room alongside.

items.name: Mayday Bar & Threesixty Bar, Hangar-7
credentials: Within Hangar-7, home to two-star Restaurant Ikarus
items.description: Two design-forward bars inside Red Bull's glass hangar, one at ground level, one suspended above the aircraft, with polished, ambitious cocktails.

plan.heading: 2 days in Salzburg, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: The old town and the fortress

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The funicular up to Hohensalzburg fortress for the whole baroque city and the mountains beyond.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Getreidegasse and Mozart's birthplace, then coffee at Café Tomaselli, the city's oldest.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the St. Peter Stiftskulinarium, said to be Europe's oldest restaurant, in the abbey walls.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Mirabell Palace and its gardens, then across the Salzach to the Residenz staterooms.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A drive out to Hellbrunn Palace for the trick fountains, or the lake country of the Salzkammergut at Fuschl.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Ikarus in Hangar-7, the rotating guest-chef table, or the Michelin room at the Schloss Fuschl if you've gone lakeside.

items.name: Altstadt (Old Town)
items.description: The UNESCO-listed core on the left bank, atmospheric but busy and central.

items.name: Neustadt / right bank
items.description: Around Mirabell Gardens and Linzergasse, a little calmer and still a short walk to everything.

items.name: Nonntal
items.description: A quiet residential pocket below the fortress for those who want to escape the crowds at night.

events.name: Mozart Week
events.note: The Mozarteum's festival around the composer's birthday, drawing leading orchestras.

events.name: Salzburg Festival
events.note: Six weeks of opera, drama and concerts, the city's cultural centrepiece.

events.name: Christmas Market on Residenzplatz
events.note: The traditional Christkindlmarkt in the cathedral square.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in the Altstadt near the Hotel Sacher or across the river at the Schloss Mönchstein for old-town access; time a visit around the summer Festspiele for the finest music, and reserve tables and tickets well in advance as the city fills.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Salzburg Airport (SZG) is minutes from the old town, and a private car makes the short transfer; many arrive instead by private car or the fast rail line from Vienna or Munich.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: The baroque old town is compact and best explored on foot; a private driver handles the lake district and Alpine excursions beyond.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Strong throughout the city and reliable into the surrounding Salzkammergut; an eSIM works on arrival.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euros (EUR); cards are widely accepted, carry a little cash for smaller establishments, and tipping runs around 5–10 percent.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May to September is green and mild for the old town and lakes, with the Salzburg Festival peaking in late July and August; December brings atmospheric Christmas markets. November and the depths of winter are wet and grey.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No long-haul flights from India; fly to Vienna (direct on Austrian or Air India, ~8h20) then about 2.5 hours by direct ÖBB or Westbahn train, or route via Munich, ~1.5 hours on by rail. The Vienna-airport-to-Salzburg train runs without a change and is the smoothest option.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations needed beyond routine; a small, very safe alpine city. Tap water is clean and drinkable throughout.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian food is easy, helped by a strong local veg and organic scene. A handful of Indian restaurants such as Way to India and Spicy Spices cover Indian and vegetarian tastes; give notice for strict Jain preparation.
